title: Shortcut text
description:
Parse shortcut text like `"Ctrl+Shift+S"` and check it against the keys held down.

```
"Ctrl+S"        -> ctrl, key S
"Ctrl+Shift+Z"  -> ctrl, shift, key Z
"Alt+F4"        -> alt, key F4
"Ctrl+"         -> invalid
held Ctrl+S -> matches "Ctrl+S", not "Ctrl+Shift+S"
```
hints: Split at `+`, upper-case each part, and set the flag for `CTRL`, `SHIFT` or `ALT`; anything else is the key (lesson 4.01).
A part that is empty (from `"Ctrl+"`) or a second key makes it invalid.
requirements: `struct Chord { bool ctrl, shift, alt; std::string key; };`
Modifiers in any order and any case; exactly one key at the end.
A match needs exactly the same modifiers (extra ones mean no match).
stretch: Format a chord back into text for the menu item's shortcut column.
